newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open mixed amid stock mkt concerns.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open mixed amid stock mkt concerns.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mixed in quiet trade on Monday, with concerns about the possibility of further weakness in equities providing support for the money market, analysts said.

"We're getting more bids here as the equities sell off," said one T-bill trader with a bank-owned brokerage. The dealer said worries about the Friday's stock market decline was encouraging some investors to seek a safe haven in the money market.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.01 percent from 3.02 percent at Friday's close.
Canadian stocks were expected to face downward pressure at the open on Monday as European markets weakened in response to Wall Street's Friday sell-off, analysts said.

"Most of the domestic accounts are keeping their maturities relatively short," said one T-bill salesman with another bank-owned brokerage. "We're not seeing much in the way of activity to start here."
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill traded unchanged from Friday to yield 3.54 percent. The one-year when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.95 percent from 3.94 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.30 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
